questions.question: Who created the Kotlin programming language?
questions.hint: Think of the company behind IntelliJ IDEA and PyCharm.
questions.explanation: Kotlin was created by JetBrains in 2011 to increase developer productivity and reduce Java verbosity.

questions.question: What is the primary motivation behind Kotlin's built-in Null Safety?
options: To speed up disk read times
To eliminate the 'Billion Dollar Mistake' (NullPointerException crashes) at compile time
To prevent developers from using integers
To convert all variables into floating-point numbers
questions.hint: Think of Tony Hoare's famous null pointer regret.
questions.explanation: Kotlin prevents NullPointerExceptions by default. Types cannot hold null unless explicitly marked with a question mark (?).

questions.question: What year did Google officially announce that Android development is 'Kotlin-first'?
questions.hint: Two years after first-class support was announced at Google I/O 2017.
questions.explanation: At Google I/O 2019, Google officially made Kotlin the preferred and recommended language for Android app development.

questions.question: How does Kotlin interact with existing Java code and libraries?
options: Kotlin cannot call Java code at all
It provides 100% two-way interoperability with zero conversion overhead
It requires an external C++ bridge to connect
It can only call Java code if Java 6 is installed
questions.hint: Both languages compile to standard JVM bytecode.
questions.explanation: Kotlin is 100% interoperable with Java. You can call Java classes from Kotlin and Kotlin classes from Java seamlessly.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to declare a function in Kotlin?
questions.hint: It is a 3-letter word that also means enjoyable.
questions.explanation: In Kotlin, functions are declared using the 'fun' keyword, as in 'fun main()'.

questions.question: What is the designated entrypoint function where a Kotlin program begins execution?
questions.hint: Think of the standard starting function name in C, C++, and Java.
questions.explanation: Every standalone Kotlin application begins execution at the top-level 'fun main()' entrypoint function.

questions.question: What is the key difference between 'val' and 'var' in Kotlin?
options: 'val' can only store numbers, 'var' can only store text
There is no difference; they are interchangeable
questions.hint: 'val' stands for value (constant) and 'var' stands for variable.
questions.explanation: 'val' creates a read-only variable whose value cannot be reassigned once initialized. 'var' creates a mutable variable.

questions.question: What is the syntax for embedding a variable inside a string template in Kotlin?
questions.hint: Think of the dollar sign symbol used in shell and bash.
questions.explanation: Kotlin uses the dollar sign '$' for string templates, e.g., 'Hello, $name' or '${expr}' for complex expressions.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP)?
options: To run Windows 95 games on Android
To share common business, data, and networking logic across platforms like Android, iOS, Desktop, and Web
To replace HTML and CSS completely in all web browsers
To compile Kotlin into hardware microchips
questions.hint: Think of sharing core application code across mobile and desktop.
questions.explanation: Kotlin Multiplatform allows developers to share non-UI business logic across Android, iOS, Desktop, and Web while maintaining native UI.

questions.question: Which of the following classes automatically provides equals(), hashCode(), and toString() in Kotlin?
questions.hint: A special class keyword specifically designed to hold data.
questions.explanation: A 'data class' in Kotlin automatically generates standard boilerplate methods like equals(), hashCode(), toString(), copy(), and componentN().
